1:   Dhritirashtra:
2:   Ranged thus for battle on the sacred plain--
3:   On Kurukshetra--say, Sanjaya! say
4:   What wrought my people, and the Pandavas?
5: 
6:   Sanjaya:
7:   When he beheld the host of Pandavas,
8:   Raja Duryodhana to Drona drew,
9:   And spake these words: "Ah, Guru! see this line,
10:   How vast it is of Pandu fighting-men,
11:   Embattled by the son of Drupada,
12:   Thy scholar in the war! Therein stand ranked
13:   Chiefs like Arjuna, like to Bhima chiefs,
14:   Benders of bows; Virata, Yuyudhan,
15:   Drupada, eminent upon his car,
16:   Dhrishtaket, Chekitan, Kasi's stout lord,
17:   Purujit, Kuntibhoj, and Saivya,
18:   With Yudhamanyu, and Uttamauj
19:   Subhadra's child; and Drupadi's;-all famed!
20:   All mounted on their shining chariots!
21:   On our side, too,--thou best of Brahmans! see
22:   Excellent chiefs, commanders of my line,
23:   Whose names I joy to count: thyself the first,
24:   Then Bhishma, Karna, Kripa fierce in fight,
25:   Vikarna, Aswatthaman; next to these
26:   Strong Saumadatti, with full many more
27:   Valiant and tried, ready this day to die
28:   For me their king, each with his weapon grasped,
29:   Each skilful in the field. Weakest-meseems-
30:   Our battle shows where Bhishma holds command,
31:   And Bhima, fronting him, something too strong!
32:   Have care our captains nigh to Bhishma's ranks
33:   Prepare what help they may! Now, blow my shell!"
34: 
35:   Then, at the signal of the aged king,
36:   With blare to wake the blood, rolling around
37:   Like to a lion's roar, the trumpeter
38:   Blew the great Conch; and, at the noise of it,
39:   Trumpets and drums, cymbals and gongs and horns
40:   Burst into sudden clamour; as the blasts
41:   Of loosened tempest, such the tumult seemed!
42:   Then might be seen, upon their car of gold
43:   Yoked with white steeds, blowing their battle-shells,
44:   Krishna the God, Arjuna at his side:
45:   Krishna, with knotted locks, blew his great conch
46:   Carved of the "Giant's bone;" Arjuna blew
47:   Indra's loud gift; Bhima the terrible--
48:   Wolf-bellied Bhima-blew a long reed-conch;
49:   And Yudhisthira, Kunti's blameless son,
50:   Winded a mighty shell, "Victory's Voice;"
51:   And Nakula blew shrill upon his conch
52:   Named the "Sweet-sounding," Sahadev on his
53:   Called"Gem-bedecked," and Kasi's Prince on his.
54:   Sikhandi on his car, Dhrishtadyumn,
55:   Virata, Satyaki the Unsubdued,
56:   Drupada, with his sons, (O Lord of Earth!)
57:   Long-armed Subhadra's children, all blew loud,
58:   So that the clangour shook their foemen's hearts,
59:   With quaking earth and thundering heav'n.
60: 
61:   Then 'twas-
62:   Beholding Dhritirashtra's battle set,
63:   Weapons unsheathing, bows drawn forth, the war
64:   Instant to break-Arjun, whose ensign-badge
65:   Was Hanuman the monkey, spake this thing
66:   To Krishna the Divine, his charioteer:
67:   "Drive, Dauntless One! to yonder open ground
68:   Betwixt the armies; I would see more nigh
69:   These who will fight with us, those we must slay
70:   To-day, in war's arbitrament; for, sure,
71:   On bloodshed all are bent who throng this plain,
72:   Obeying Dhritirashtra's sinful son."
73: 
74:   Thus, by Arjuna prayed, (O Bharata!)
75:   Between the hosts that heavenly Charioteer
76:   Drove the bright car, reining its milk-white steeds
77:   Where Bhishma led,and Drona,and their Lords.
78:   "See!" spake he to Arjuna, "where they stand,
79:   Thy kindred of the Kurus:" and the Prince
80:   Marked on each hand the kinsmen of his house,
81:   Grandsires and sires, uncles and brothers and sons,
82:   Cousins and sons-in-law and nephews, mixed
83:   With friends and honoured elders; some this side,
84:   Some that side ranged: and, seeing those opposed,
85:   Such kith grown enemies-Arjuna's heart
86:   Melted with pity, while he uttered this:
87: 
88:   Arjuna.
89:   Krishna! as I behold, come here to shed
90:   Their common blood, yon concourse of our kin,
91:   My members fail, my tongue dries in my mouth,
92:   A shudder thrills my body, and my hair
93:   Bristles with horror; from my weak hand slips
94:   Gandiv, the goodly bow; a fever burns
95:   My skin to parching; hardly may I stand;
96:   The life within me seems to swim and faint;
97:   Nothing do I foresee save woe and wail!
98:   It is not good, O Keshav! nought of good
99:   Can spring from mutual slaughter! Lo, I hate
100:   Triumph and domination, wealth and ease,
101:   Thus sadly won! Aho! what victory
102:   Can bring delight, Govinda! what rich spoils
103:   Could profit; what rule recompense; what span
104:   Of life itself seem sweet, bought with such blood?
105:   Seeing that these stand here, ready to die,
106:   For whose sake life was fair, and pleasure pleased,
107:   And power grew precious:-grandsires, sires, and sons,
108:   Brothers, and fathers-in-law, and sons-in-law,
109:   Elders and friends! Shall I deal death on these
110:   Even though they seek to slay us? Not one blow,
111:   O Madhusudan! will I strike to gain
112: 
113:   The rule of all Three Worlds; then, how much less
114:   To seize an earthly kingdom! Killing these
115:   Must breed but anguish, Krishna! If they be
116:   Guilty, we shall grow guilty by their deaths;
117:   Their sins will light on us, if we shall slay
118:   Those sons of Dhritirashtra, and our kin;
119:   What peace could come of that, O Madhava?
120:   For if indeed, blinded by lust and wrath,
121:   These cannot see, or will not see, the sin
122:   Of kingly lines o'erthrown and kinsmen slain,
123:   How should not we, who see, shun such a crime--
124:   We who perceive the guilt and feel the shame--
125:   O thou Delight of Men, Janardana?
126:   By overthrow of houses perisheth
127:   Their sweet continuous household piety,
128:   And-rites neglected, piety extinct--
129:   Enters impiety upon that home;
130:   Its women grow unwomaned, whence there spring
131:   Mad passions, and the mingling-up of castes,
132:   Sending a Hell-ward road that family,
133:   And whoso wrought its doom by wicked wrath.
134:   Nay, and the souls of honoured ancestors
135:   Fall from their place of peace, being bereft
136:   Of funeral-cakes and the wan death-water.[FN#1]
137:   So teach our holy hymns. Thus, if we slay
138:   Kinsfolk and friends for love of earthly power,
139:   Ahovat! what an evil fault it were!
140:   Better I deem it, if my kinsmen strike,
141:   To face them weaponless, and bare my breast
142:   To shaft and spear, than answer blow with blow.
143: 
144:   So speaking, in the face of those two hosts,
145:   Arjuna sank upon his chariot-seat,
146:   And let fall bow and arrows, sick at heart.
147: 
148:   HERE ENDETH CHAPTER I. OF THE BHAGAVAD-GITA,
149:   Entitled "Arjun-Vishad,"
150:   Or "The Book of the Distress of Arjuna."

witnesses.text: 1.12 The valiant grandfather, the eldest of the Kurus, loudly sounding a lion-roar, blew the conch to raise his (Duryodhana's) spirits.

records.sanskrit:
ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च पणवानकगोमुखाः।
सहसैवाभ्यहन्यन्त स शब्दस्तुमुलोऽभवत् ॥
records.iast:
tataḥ śaṅkhāśca bheryaśca paṇavānakagomukhāḥ
sahasaivābhyahanyanta sa śabdastumulo.abhavat
records.speaker: Sanjaya

arnold.content:
and, at the noise of it,
  Trumpets and drums, cymbals and gongs and horns
  Burst into sudden clamour; as the blasts
  Of loosened tempest, such the tumult seemed!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.13. Then (following Bhishma), conches and kettledrums, tabors,
drums and cow horns blared forth ite suddenly (from the Kaurava side)
and the sound was tremendous.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.13 And immediately all the conches and drums, the trumpets and horns, blared forth in tumultuous uproar.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.13 Just immediately after that conchs and kettledrums, and tabors, trumpets and cow-horns blared forth. That sound became tumultuous.

records.sanskrit:
ततः श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते महति स्यन्दने स्थितौ।
माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रदध्मतुः ॥
records.iast:
tataḥ śvetairhayairyukte mahati syandane sthitau
mādhavaḥ pāṇḍavaścaiva divyau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ
records.speaker: Sanjaya

arnold.content:
Then might be seen, upon their car of gold
  Yoked with white steeds, blowing their battle-shells,
  Krishna the God, Arjuna at his side:

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.14. Then, also, Madhava (Krishna) and the son of Pandu (Arjuna),
seated in the magnificent chariot, yoked with white horses, blew divine
conches.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.14 Then seated in their spacious war chariot, yoked with white horses, Lord Shri Krishna and Arjuna sounded their divine shells.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.14 Then, Madhava (Krsna) and the son of Pandu (Arjuna), stationed in their magnificent chariot with white horses yoked to it, loudly blew their divine conchs.

records.sanskrit:
पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनञ्जयः।
पौण्ड्रं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः ॥
records.iast:
pāñcajanyaṃ hṛṣīkeśo devadattaṃ dhanañjayaḥ
pauṇḍraṃ dadhmau mahāśaṅkhaṃ bhīmakarmā vṛkodaraḥ
records.speaker: Sanjaya

arnold.content:
Krishna, with knotted locks, blew his great conch
  Carved of the "Giant's bone;" Arjuna blew
  Indra's loud gift; Bhima the terrible--
  Wolf-bellied Bhima-blew a long reed-conch;

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.15. Hrishikesha blew the Panchajanya and Arjuna blew the Devadatta
and Bhima (the wolf-bellied), the doer of terrible deeds, blew the great
conch Paundra.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.15 Lord Shri Krishna blew his Panchajanya and Arjuna his Devadatta, brave Bheema his renowned shell, Poundra.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.15 Hrsikesa (Krsna) (blew the conch) Pancajanya; Dhananjaya (Arjuna) (the conch) Devadatta; and Vrkodara (Bhima) of terrible deeds blew the great conch Paundra;

records.sanskrit:
अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः।
नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ ॥
records.iast:
anantavijayaṃ rājā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
nakulaḥ sahadevaśca sughoṣamaṇipuṣpakau
records.speaker: Sanjaya

arnold.content:
And Yudhisthira, Kunti's blameless son,
  Winded a mighty shell, "Victory's Voice;"
  And Nakula blew shrill upon his conch
  Named the "Sweet-sounding," Sahadev on his
  Called"Gem-bedecked,"

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.16. The king Yodhishthira, the son of Kunti, blew the Anantavijaya;
Nakula and Sahadeva blew the Sughosha and the Manipushpaka.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.16 The King Dharmaraja, the son of Kunti, blew the Anantavijaya, Nakalu and Sahadeo, the Sugosh and Manipushpaka, respectively.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.16 King Yudhisthira, son of Kunti, (blew) the Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva, the Sughosa and the Manipuspaka (respectively).

records.sanskrit:
काश्यश्च परमेष्वासः शिखण्डी च महारथः।
धृष्टद्युम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्चापराजितः ॥
records.iast:
kāśyaśca parameṣvāsaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahārathaḥ
dhṛṣṭadyumno virāṭaśca sātyakiścāparājitaḥ
records.speaker: Sanjaya

arnold.content:
and Kasi's Prince on his.
  Sikhandi on his car, Dhrishtadyumn,
  Virata, Satyaki the Unsubdued,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.17. The king of Kasi, an exellent archer, Sikhandi, the mighty
car-warrior, Dhrishtadyumna and Virata and Satyaki, the unconered.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.17 And the Maharaja of Benares, the great archer, Shikhandi, the great soldier, Dhrishtayumna, Virata and Satyaki, the invincible,

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.17 And the King of Kasi, wielding a great bow, and the great chariot-rider Sikhandi, Dhrstadyumna and Virata, and Satyaki the unconered;

records.sanskrit:
द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते।
सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक् ॥
records.iast:
drupado draupadeyāśca sarvaśaḥ pṛthivīpate
saubhadraśca mahābāhuḥ śaṅkhāndadhmuḥ pṛthakpṛthak
records.speaker: Sanjaya

arnold.content:
Drupada, with his sons, (O Lord of Earth!)
  Long-armed Subhadra's children, all blew loud,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.18. Drupada and the sons of Draupadi, O Lord of the earth, and
the son of Subhadra, the mighty-armed, blew their conches separately.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.18 And O King! Drupada, the sons of Droupadi and Soubhadra, the great soldier, blew their conches.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.18 Drupada and the sons of Draupadi, and the son of Subhadra, (Abhimanyu) the mighty-armed all (of them) together, O king, blew their respective conchs.

records.sanskrit:
स घोषो धार्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत्।
नभश्च पृथिवीं चैव तुमुलोऽभ्यनुनादयन् (or लोव्यनु) ॥
records.iast:
sa ghoṣo dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ hṛdayāni vyadārayat
nabhaśca pṛthivīṃ caiva tumulo.abhyanunādayan (lo vyanu)
records.speaker: Sanjaya

arnold.content:
So that the clangour shook their foemen's hearts,
  With quaking earth and thundering heav'n.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.19. That tumultuous sound rent the hearts of (the members of)
Dhritarashtra's party, making both the heaven and the earth resound.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.19 The tumult rent the hearts of the sons of Dhritarashtra, and violently shook heaven and earth with its echo.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.19 That tremendous sound pierced the hearts of the sons of Dhrtarastra as it reverberated through the sky and the earth.

records.sanskrit:
अथ व्यवस्थितान्दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान् कपिध्वजः।
प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः।
हृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते ॥
records.iast:
atha vyavasthitāndṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapidhvajaḥ
pravṛtte śastrasampāte dhanurudyamya pāṇḍavaḥ
records.speaker: Sanjaya

arnold.content:
Then 'twas-
  Beholding Dhritirashtra's battle set,
  Weapons unsheathing, bows drawn forth, the war
  Instant to break-Arjun, whose ensign-badge
  Was Hanuman the monkey, spake this thing
  To Krishna the Divine, his charioteer:

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.20. Then, seeing the people of Dhritarashtra’s party standing
arrayed and the discharge of weapons about to begin, Arjuna, the son of
Pandu, whose ensign was a monkey, took up his bow and said the following
to Krishna, O Lord of the earth.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.20 Then beholding the sons of Dhritarashtra, drawn up on the battle- field, ready to fight, Arjuna, whose flag bore the Hanuman,

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.20 O king, thereafter, seeing Dhrtarastra's men standing in their positions, when all the weapons were ready for action, the son of Pandu (Arjuna) who had the insignia of Hanuman of his chariot-flag, raising up his bow, said the following to Hrsikesa.

records.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मेऽच्युत ॥
records.iast:
hṛṣīkeśaṃ tadā vākyamidamāha mahīpate
arjuna uvāca
senayorubhayormadhye rathaṃ sthāpaya me.acyuta
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
"Drive, Dauntless One! to yonder open ground
  Betwixt the armies;

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.21 Arjuna said In the middle between the two armies, place my chariot,
O krishna, so that I may behold those who stand here desirous to fight,
and know with whom I must fight, when the battle is about to commence.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.21 Raising his bow, spoke this to the Lord Shri Krishna: O Infallible! Lord of the earth! Please draw up my chariot betwixt the two armies,

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.21 Arjuna said O Acyuta, please place my chariot between both the armies .

records.sanskrit:
यावदेतान्निरीक्षेऽहं योद्धुकामानवस्थितान्।
कैर्मया सह योद्धव्यमस्मिन् रणसमुद्यमे ॥
records.iast:
yāvadetānnirikṣe.ahaṃ yoddhukāmānavasthitān
kairmayā saha yoddhavyamasmin raṇasamudyame
records.speaker: Arjuna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.22. Arjuna said In the middle between the two armies, place my chariot,
O krishna, so that I may behold those who stand here desirous to fight,
and know with whom I must fight, when the battle is about to commence.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.22 So that I may observe those who must fight on my side, those who must fight against me;

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.22 until I survey these who stand intent on fighting, and those who are going to engage in battle with me in this impending war.

records.sanskrit:
योत्स्यमानानवेक्षेऽहं य एतेऽत्र समागताः।
धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्युद्धे प्रियचिकीर्षवः ॥
records.iast:
yotsyamānānavekṣe.ahaṃ ya ete.atra samāgatāḥ
dhārtarāṣṭrasya durbuddheryuddhe priyacikīrṣavaḥ
records.speaker: Arjuna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.23. For I desire to observe those who are assembled here to fight,
wishing to please in battle the evil-minded Duryodhana (the son of Dhritarashtra).

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.23 And gaze over this array of soldiers, eager to please the sinful sons of Dhritarashtra."

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.23 These who have assembled here and want to accomplish in the war what is dear to the perverted son of Dhrtarastra, I find them to be intent on fighting.

records.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
एवमुक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम् ॥
records.iast:
sañjaya uvāca
evamukto hṛṣīkeśo guḍākeśena bhārata
senayorubhayormadhye sthāpayitvā rathottamam
records.speaker: Sanjaya

arnold.content:
Thus, by Arjuna prayed, (O Bharata!)
  Between the hosts that heavenly Charioteer
  Drove the bright car, reining its milk-white steeds

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.24. Sanjaya said Thus addressed by Arjuna, Krishna, having stationed that
best of chariots, O Dhritarashtra, in the midst of the two armies.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.24 Sanjaya said: "Having listened to the request of Arjuna, Lord Shri Krishna drew up His bright chariot exactly in the midst between the two armies,

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.24 1.25 Sanjay said O scion of the line of Bharata (Dhrtararastra), Hrsikesa, being told so by Gudakesa (Arjuna), placed the excellent chariot between the two armies, in front of Bhisma and Drona as also all the rulers of the earth, and said, 'O Partha (Arjuna), see these assempled people of the Kuru dynasty.'

records.sanskrit:
भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम्।
उवाच पार्थ पश्यैतान्समवेतान्कुरूनिति ॥
records.iast:
bhīṣmadroṇapramukhataḥ sarveṣāṃ ca mahīkṣitām
uvāca pārtha paśyaitānsamavetānkurūniti
records.speaker: Sanjaya

arnold.content:
Where Bhishma led,and Drona,and their Lords.
  "See!" spake he to Arjuna, "where they stand,
  Thy kindred of the Kurus:"

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.25. In front of Bhishma and Drona, and all the rulers of the
earth, said: "O Arjuna (son of Pritha), behold these Kurus gathered together."

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.25 Whither Bheeshma and Drona had led all the rulers of the earth, and spoke thus: O Arjuna! Behold these members of the family of Kuru assembled.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.24 1.25 Sanjay said O scion of the line of Bharata (Dhrtararastra), Hrsikesa, being told so by Gudakesa (Arjuna), placed the excellent chariot between the two armies, in front of Bhisma and Drona as also all the rulers of the earth, and said, 'O Partha (Arjuna), see these assempled people of the Kuru dynasty.'

records.sanskrit:
तत्रापश्यत्स्थितान्पार्थः पितॄनथ पितामहान्।
आचार्यान्मातुलान्भ्रातॄन्पुत्रान्पौत्रान्सखींस्तथा ॥
records.iast:
tatrāpaśyatsthitānpārthaḥ pitṝnatha pitāmahān
ācāryānmātulānbhrātṛnputrānpautrānsakhīṃstathā
records.speaker: Sanjaya

arnold.content:
and the Prince
  Marked on each hand the kinsmen of his house,
  Grandsires and sires, uncles and brothers and sons,
  Cousins and sons-in-law and nephews, mixed
  With friends and honoured elders; some this side,
  Some that side ranged: and, seeing those opposed,
  Such kith grown enemies-Arjuna's heart
  Melted with pity, while he uttered this:

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.26. Then, Arjuna (son of Pritha) saw there (in the armies) stationed,
fathers and grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons
and friends too.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.26 There Arjuna noticed fathers, grandfathers, uncles, cousins, sons, grandsons, teachers, friends;

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.26 Then Partha (Arjuna) saw, marshalled among both the armies, (his) uncles as also grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers (and (cousins), sons, grandsons, as well as comrades and fathers-in-law and friends.

records.sanskrit:
श्वशुरान्सुहृदश्चैव सेनयोरुभयोरपि।
तान्समीक्ष्य स कौन्तेयः सर्वान्बन्धूनवस्थितान् ॥
records.iast:
śvaśurānsuhṛdaścaiva senayorubhayorapi
tānsamīkṣya sa kaunteyaḥ sarvānbandhūnavasthitān
records.speaker: Sanjaya

arnold.content:
and the Prince
  Marked on each hand the kinsmen of his house,
  Grandsires and sires, uncles and brothers and sons,
  Cousins and sons-in-law and nephews, mixed
  With friends and honoured elders; some this side,
  Some that side ranged: and, seeing those opposed,
  Such kith grown enemies-Arjuna's heart
  Melted with pity, while he uttered this:

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.27. (He saw) fathers-in-law and friends also in both the armies.
The son of Kunti, Arjuna, seeing all those kinsmen thus standing arrayed,
spoke this, sorrowfully filled with deep pity.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.27 Fathers-in-law and benefactors, arrayed on both sides. Arjuna then gazed at all those kinsmen before him.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.27 The son of Kunti (Ajuna), seeing all those rlatives arrayed (there), became overwhelmed by supreme compassion and said this sorrowfully:

records.sanskrit:
कृपया परयाविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत्।
अर्जुन उवाच।
दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥
records.iast:
kṛpayā parayāviṣṭo viṣīdannidamabravīt
arjuna uvāca
dṛṣṭvemaṃ svajanaṃ kṛṣṇa yuyutsuṃ samupasthitam
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
Arjuna.
  Krishna! as I behold, come here to shed
  Their common blood, yon concourse of our kin,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 1.28. Arjuna said Seeing these, my kinsmen, O krishna, arrayed, eager to fight.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.28 And his heart melted with pity and sadly he spoke: O my Lord! When I see all these, my own people, thirsting for battle,

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.28 Arjuna said O Krsna, seeing these relatives and friends who have assembled here with the intention of fighting, my limbs become languid and my mouth becomes completely dry.

records.sanskrit:
सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति।
वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥
records.iast:
sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati
vepathuśca śarīre me romaharṣaśca jāyate
records.speaker: Arjuna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.29. My limbs fail and my mouth is parched, my body ivers and
my hair stands on end.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.29 My limbs fail me and my throat is parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.29 And there is trembling in my body, and there is horripillation; the Gandiva (bow) slips from the hand and even the skin burns intensely.

records.sanskrit:
गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते।
न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥
records.iast:
gāṇḍīvaṃ sraṃsate hastāttvakcaiva paridahyate
na ca śaknomyavasthātuṃ bhramatīva ca me manaḥ
records.speaker: Arjuna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.30. The (bow) Gandiva slips from my hand, and also my skins burns
all over; I am unable even to stand and my mind is reeling, as it were.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.30 The bow Gandeeva slips from my hand, and my skin burns. I cannot keep quiet, for my mind is in tumult.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.30 Moreover, O Kesava (Krsna), I am not able to stand firmly, and my mind seems to be whirling. And I notice the omens to be adverse.

records.sanskrit:
निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव।
न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे ॥
records.iast:
nimittāni ca paśyāmi viparītāni keśava
na ca śreyo.anupaśyāmi hatvā svajanamāhave
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
Nothing do I foresee save woe and wail!
  It is not good, O Keshav! nought of good
  Can spring from mutual slaughter!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.31. And I see adverse omens, O Kesava. I do not see any good
in killing my kinsmen in battle.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.31 The omens are adverse; what good can come from the slaughter of my people on this battlefield?

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.31 Besides, I do not see any good (to be derived) from killing my own people in battle. O Krsna, I do not hanker after victory, nor even a kingdom nor pleasures.

records.sanskrit:
न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च।
किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा ॥
records.iast:
na kāṅkṣe vijayaṃ kṛṣṇa na ca rājyaṃ sukhāni ca
kiṃ no rājyena govinda kiṃ bhogairjīvitena vā
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
Lo, I hate
  Triumph and domination, wealth and ease,
  Thus sadly won! Aho! what victory
  Can bring delight, Govinda! what rich spoils
  Could profit; what rule recompense; what span
  Of life itself seem sweet, bought with such blood?

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.32. I desire not victory, O Krishna, nor kingdom, nor pleasures.
Of what avail is dominion to us, O Krishna, or pleasures or even life?

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.32 Ah my Lord! I crave not for victory, nor for the kingdom, nor for any pleasure. What were a kingdom or happiness or life to me,

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.32 1.34 O Govinda! What need do we have of a kingdom, or what (need) of enjoyments and livelihood? Those for whom kingdom, enjoyments and pleasures ae desired by us, viz teachers, uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law as also relatives-those very ones stand arrayed for battle risking their lives and wealth.

records.sanskrit:
येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च।
त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च ॥
records.iast:
yeṣāmarthe kāṅkṣitaṃ no rājyaṃ bhogāḥ sukhāni ca
ta ime.avasthitā yuddhe prāṇāṃstyaktvā dhanāni ca
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
Seeing that these stand here, ready to die,
  For whose sake life was fair, and pleasure pleased,
  And power grew precious:-

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.33. Those for whose sake we desire kingdom, enjoyments and pleasures,
stand here in battle, having renounced life and wealth.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.33 When those for whose sake I desire these things stand here about to sacrifice their property and their lives:

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.32 1.34 O Govinda! What need do we have of a kingdom, or what (need) of enjoyments and livelihood? Those for whom kingdom, enjoyments and pleasures ae desired by us, viz teachers, uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law as also relatives-those very ones stand arrayed for battle risking their lives and wealth.

records.sanskrit:
आचार्याः पितरः पुत्रास्तथैव च पितामहाः।
मातुलाः श्वशुराः पौत्राः श्यालाः सम्बन्धिनस्तथा ॥
records.iast:
ācāryāḥ pitaraḥ putrāstathaiva ca pitāmahāḥ
mātulāḥ śvaśurāḥ pautrāḥ śyālāḥ sambandhinastathā
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
grandsires, sires, and sons,
  Brothers, and fathers-in-law, and sons-in-law,
  Elders and friends!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.34. Teachers, fathers, sons and also grandfathers, maternal uncles,
fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law and other relatives,-

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.34 Teachers, fathers and grandfathers, sons and grandsons, uncles, father-in-law, brothers-in-law and other relatives.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.32 1.34 O Govinda! What need do we have of a kingdom, or what (need) of enjoyments and livelihood? Those for whom kingdom, enjoyments and pleasures ae desired by us, viz teachers, uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law as also relatives-those very ones stand arrayed for battle risking their lives and wealth.

records.sanskrit:
एतान्न हन्तुमिच्छामि घ्नतोऽपि मधुसूदन।
अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते ॥
records.iast:
etānna hantumicchāmi ghnato.api madhusūdana
api trailokyarājyasya hetoḥ kiṃ nu mahīkṛte
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
Shall I deal death on these
  Even though they seek to slay us? Not one blow,
  O Madhusudan! will I strike to gain

  The rule of all Three Worlds; then, how much less
  To seize an earthly kingdom!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.35. These I do not wish to kill, though they kill me, O Krishna,
even for the sake of dominion over the three worlds; leave alone killing
them for the sake of the earth.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.35 I would not kill them, even for three worlds; why then for this poor earth? It matters not if I myself am killed.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.35 O Madhusudana, even if I am killed, I do not want to kill these even for the sake of a kingdom extending over the three worlds; what to speak of doing so for the earth!

records.sanskrit:
निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन।
पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः ॥
records.iast:
nihatya dhārtarāṣṭrānnaḥ kā prītiḥ syājjanārdana
pāpamevāśrayedasmānhatvaitānātatāyinaḥ
records.speaker: Arjuna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.36. By killing these sons of Dhritarashtra, what pleasure can
be ours, O Janardana? Only sin will accrue to us from killing these felons.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.36 My Lord! What happiness can come from the death of these sons of Dhritarashtra? We shall sin if we kill these desperate men.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.36 O Janardana, what happiness shall we derive by killing the sons of Dhrtarastra? Sin alone will accrue to us by killing these felons.

records.sanskrit:
तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान्।
स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव ॥
records.iast:
tasmānnārhā vayaṃ hantuṃ dhārtarāṣṭrānsvabāndhavān
svajanaṃ hi kathaṃ hatvā sukhinaḥ syāma mādhava
records.speaker: Arjuna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.37. Therefore, we should not kill the sons of Dhritarashtra,
our relatives; for how can we be happy by killing our own people, O Madhava
(Krishna)?

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.37 We are worthy of a nobler feat than to slaughter our relatives - the sons of Dhritarashtra; for, my Lord, how can we be happy of we kill our kinsmen?

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.37 Therefore, it is not proper for us to kill the sons of Dhrtarastra who are our own relatives. For, O Madhava, how can we be happy by killing our kinsmen?

records.sanskrit:
यद्यप्येते न पश्यन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः।
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम् ॥
records.iast:
yadyapyete na paśyanti lobhopahatacetasaḥ
kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ mitradrohe ca pātakam
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
For if indeed, blinded by lust and wrath,
  These cannot see, or will not see, the sin
  Of kingly lines o'erthrown and kinsmen slain,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.38. Though they, with intelligence overpowered by greed, see
no evil in the destruction of families, and no sin in hostility to friends,

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.38 Although these men, blinded by greed, see no guilt in destroying their kin, or fighting against their friends,

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.38 1.39 O Janardana, although these people, whose hearts have become perverted by greed, do not see the evil arising from destroying the family and sin in hostility towards, friends, yet how can we who clearly see the evil arising from destroying the family remain unaware of (the need of) abstaining from this sin?

records.sanskrit:
कथं न ज्ञेयमस्माभिः पापादस्मान्निवर्तितुम्।
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपश्यद्भिर्जनार्दन ॥
records.iast:
kathaṃ na jñeyamasmābhiḥ pāpādasmānnivartitum
kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ prapaśyadbhirjanārdana
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
How should not we, who see, shun such a crime--
  We who perceive the guilt and feel the shame--
  O thou Delight of Men, Janardana?

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.39. Why should not we who clearly see evil in the destruction
of families, learn to turn away from this sin, O Janardana (Krishna)?

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.39 Should not we, whose eyes are open, who consider it to be wrong to annihilate our house, turn away from so great a crime?

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.38 1.39 O Janardana, although these people, whose hearts have become perverted by greed, do not see the evil arising from destroying the family and sin in hostility towards, friends, yet how can we who clearly see the evil arising from destroying the family remain unaware of (the need of) abstaining from this sin?

records.sanskrit:
कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्माः सनातनाः।
धर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्मोऽभिभवत्युत ॥
records.iast:
kulakṣaye praṇaśyanti kuladharmāḥ sanātanāḥ
dharme naṣṭe kulaṃ kṛtsnamadharmo.abhibhavatyuta
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
By overthrow of houses perisheth
  Their sweet continuous household piety,
  And-rites neglected, piety extinct--
  Enters impiety upon that home;

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.40. In the destruction of a family, the immemorial religious
rites of that family perish; on the destruction of spirituality, impiety,
indeed, overcomes the whole family.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.40 The destruction of our kindred means the destruction of the traditions of our ancient lineage, and when these are lost, irreligion will overrun our homes.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.40 From the ruin of the family are totally destroyed the traditional rites and duties of the family. When rites and duties are destroyed, vice overpowers the entire family also.

records.sanskrit:
अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः।
स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसङ्करः ॥
records.iast:
adharmābhibhavātkṛṣṇa praduṣyanti kulastriyaḥ
strīṣu duṣṭāsu vārṣṇeya jāyate varṇasaṅkaraḥ
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
Its women grow unwomaned, whence there spring
  Mad passions, and the mingling-up of castes,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.41. By the prevalence of impiety, O Krishna, the women of
the family become corrupt; and , women being corrupted, O Varshenya (descendant
of Vrishni), there arises intermingling of castes.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.41 When irreligion spreads, the women of the house begin to stray; when they lose their purity, adulteration of the stock follows.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.41 O Krsna, when vice predominates, the women of the family become corrupt. O descendent of the Vrsnis, when women become corrupted, it results in the intermingling of castes.

records.sanskrit:
सङ्करो नरकायैव कुलघ्नानां कुलस्य च।
पतन्ति पितरो ह्येषां लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः ॥
records.iast:
saṅkaro narakāyaiva kulaghnānāṃ kulasya ca
patanti pitaro hyeṣāṃ luptapiṇḍodakakriyāḥ
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
Sending a Hell-ward road that family,
  And whoso wrought its doom by wicked wrath.
  Nay, and the souls of honoured ancestors
  Fall from their place of peace, being bereft
  Of funeral-cakes and the wan death-water.[FN#1]

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.42. Confusion of castes leads to hell the slayers of the family,
for their forefathers fall, deprived of the offerings of rice-ball and
water (libations).

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.42 Promiscuity ruins both the family and those who defile it; while the souls of our ancestors droop, through lack of the funeral cakes and ablutions.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.42 And the intermingling in the family leads the ruiners of the family verily into hell. The forefathers of these fall down (into hell) because of being deprived of the offerings of rice-balls and water.

records.sanskrit:
दोषैरेतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसङ्करकारकैः।
उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्माः कुलधर्माश्च शाश्वताः ॥
records.iast:
doṣairetaiḥ kulaghnānāṃ varṇasaṅkarakārakaiḥ
utsādyante jātidharmāḥ kuladharmāśca śāśvatāḥ
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.note: Arnold omits the repeated statement about the destruction of family and caste rites; note 1 explicitly records omitted repetitionary lines.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.43. By these evil deeds of the destroyers of the family, which
cause confusion of castes, the eternal religious rites of the caste and
the family are destroyed.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.43 By the destruction of our lineage and the pollution of blood, ancient class traditions and family purity alike perish.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.43 Due to these misdeeds of the ruiners of the family, which cause intermingling of castes, the traditional rites and duties of the castes and families become destroyed.

records.sanskrit:
उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्दन।
नरके नियतं वासो भवतीत्यनुशुश्रुम (or नरकेऽनियतं) ॥
records.iast:
utsannakuladharmāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ janārdana
narake niyataṃ vāso bhavatītyanuśuśruma
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content: So teach our holy hymns.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.44. We have heard, O Janardana, that inevitable is the dwelling
for an unknown period in hell for those men in whose families the religious
practices have been destroyed.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.44 The wise say, my Lord, that they are forever lost, whose ancient traditions are lost.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.44 O Janardana, we have heard that living in hell becomes inevitable for those persons whose family duties get destroyed.

records.sanskrit:
अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम्।
यद्राज्यसुखलोभेन हन्तुं स्वजनमुद्यताः ॥
records.iast:
aho bata mahatpāpaṃ kartuṃ vyavasitā vayam
yadrājyasukhalobhena hantuṃ svajanamudyatāḥ
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
Thus, if we slay
  Kinsfolk and friends for love of earthly power,
  Ahovat! what an evil fault it were!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.45. Alas! We are involved in a great sin, in that we are
prepared to kill our kinsmen, through greed for the pleasures of a kingdom.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.45 Alas, it is strange that we should be willing to kill our own countrymen and commit a great sin, in order to enjoy the pleasures of a kingdom.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.45 What a pity that we have resolved to commit a great sin by being eager to kill our own kith and kin, out of greed for the pleasures of a kingdom!

records.sanskrit:
यदि मामप्रतीकारमशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः।
धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत् ॥
records.iast:
yadi māmapratīkāramaśastraṃ śastrapāṇayaḥ
dhārtarāṣṭrā raṇe hanyustanme kṣemataraṃ bhavet
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
Better I deem it, if my kinsmen strike,
  To face them weaponless, and bare my breast
  To shaft and spear, than answer blow with blow.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.46. If the sons of Dhritarashtra with weapons in hand should
slay me in battle, unresisting and unarmed, that would be better for me.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.46 If, on the contrary, the sons of Dhritarashtra, with weapons in their hand, should slay me, unarmed and unresisting, surely that would be better for my welfare!"

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.46 If, in this battle, the sons of Dhrtarastra armed with weapons kill me who am non-resistant and unarmed, that will be more beneficial to me.

records.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
एवमुक्त्वार्जुनः सङ्ख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत्।
विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥
records.iast:
sañjaya uvāca
evamuktvārjunaḥ saṅkhye rathopastha upāviśat
visṛjya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ śokasaṃvignamānasaḥ
records.speaker: Sanjaya

arnold.content:
So speaking, in the face of those two hosts,
  Arjuna sank upon his chariot-seat,
  And let fall bow and arrows, sick at heart.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
1.47. Sanjaya said Having thus spoken in the midst of the battlefield, Arjuna,
casting away his bow and arrow, sat down on the seat of the chariot with
his mind overwhelmed with sorrow.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 1.47 Sanjaya said: "Having spoken thus, in the midst of the armies, Arjuna sank on the seat of the chariot, casting away his bow and arrow; heartbroken with grief."

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 1.47 Sanjaya narrated: Having said so, Arjuna, with a mind afflicted with sorrow, sat down on the chariot in the midst of the battle, casting aside the bow along with the arrows.
